objective: Proof. (i) Every nontrivial 2-edge cut of a cubic incidence graph is balanced: each side has as many points as lines, one port point and one slot line. (ii) In a knot's space, cutting either edge of a 2-edge cut leaves an atom, an exact negation (KNOT-COUPLING A), so the two sides act as permutations of {0,1} whose composite is a negation: one side is equality, the other disequality, complementary two-place parity. (iii) Across every nontrivial 3-edge cut the sides are not-all-equal and equality (KNOT-COMPOSE A). So the knot's spaces compose through hubs across 3-edge cuts and without hubs, by parity, across 2-edge cuts; odd cycles of Fano blocks and the twisted cube have 2-edge cuts. This corrects KNOT-COMPOSE's headline.
status: Proved by NATIVE-PATHS-20261101-001A-P001: across every nontrivial 2-edge cut of a knot's space one shore accepts exactly equality and the other exactly disequality (complementary two-place parity, no hub); across every nontrivial 3-edge cut the point side accepts exactly one antipodal pair {v, v-bar} and the line side its complement (equality against not-all-equal up to an exchange of colours on some channels); corrects KNOT-COMPOSE-20261101-001A ('compose only through hubs' fails at 2-edge cuts, present in odd cycles of Fano blocks and the twisted cube; 'exactly' holds only up to signs); 40 two-edge and 48 three-edge cuts checked on ten spaces
title: Two kinds of interface: parity across 2-edge cuts, knot against hub across 3-edge cuts
